heuristic.applicability: Prefer when block and destination are within the demonstrated geometric corridor but current TCP/object height, lag, or release timing differs from a nominal trajectory, and two causal frames provide consistent phase evidence. It is useful in the 900:1160 overlap for deciding whether to hold, open, retreat, or present at the handle. Do not prefer it for a large rigid displacement of the held block or drawer; those are covered by the object- and destination-frame priors.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer open/stable; observations and measured joints valid; block plausibly attached for carry entry or visibly in the cavity/release corridor for mid-skill entry; current state is not an unseen drop recovery.
handoff.exit_conditions: Causal geometry indicates object stationary at drawer-floor height and detached, TCP has retreated, and preferably the gripper has reached the handle approach for close_drawer.
handoff.failure_signatures: Auxiliary phase conflicts with observed object/TCP motion, object stops following before release, open command occurs while outside the cavity, object continues to follow after opening, local deltas repeatedly grow/drift, or IK reports nonconvergence/limits.
handoff.overlap_role: All 680:1160 actions are supervised. The 680:840 overlap admits predecessor variation; the large 900:1160 overlap explicitly trains opening, settling holds, retreat, reorientation, handle approach and re-closing.
handoff.successor_readiness: Transfer to close_drawer only when observed object height/motion supports deposited-retreat or handle-ready, not from the auxiliary class alone. Preserve two-frame history across the switch. Late transfer is at the handle.

heuristic.limitations: Current-TCP increments can accumulate error and do not make global object/destination displacements invariant. Stage labels are coarse, derived from demonstrated action/geometry, and cannot establish contact; unseen failure recovery is unsupported. Two frames may be insufficient for noisy or occluded settling. Rotation-vector labels can be difficult near pi, though demonstrated per-step relative targets are local. IK and collision feasibility remain required.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: The high-level agent chooses this local policy at perturbed intermediate states with reliable observations. It can take over from either invariant-frame policy in the fully supervised slice, and transfer to close_drawer after deposited-retreat/handle-ready evidence. If the whole object pose is displaced while attached, select object-frame; if the fixture/goal is displaced, select destination-frame. The auxiliary stage is advisory and is not a contact detector or success predicate.
heuristic.rationale: Observed: the skill contains distinct but adjacent modes—closed carry/descent (680-900), opening and variable settling timing (demo12100 910-920, demo12102 900-905, demo12104 895-900), open upward retreat (920-960), and handle approach/re-closing (1080-1159). The same spatial neighborhood around the drawer therefore supports different gripper and motion commands. Likely deployment failure: a predecessor or chunk boundary enters at an intermediate state, and a globally parameterized policy confuses descent, settling, or retreat. Mechanism: action labels are one-step targets relative to each pre-action measured TCP, so fresh-state decoding acts as local feedback; two causal frames expose object-following and motion; a four-stage auxiliary classifier regularizes the shared trainable condition latent that directly conditions the unchanged DP backbone. Expected benefit is improved local correction and phase separation, not demonstrated recovery.
heuristic.statement: Phase-aware local Cartesian corrections: diffuse each commanded target as a current-TCP-frame translation increment (m), rotation vector (rad), and gripper scalar, decoded from the fresh measured TCP at each slot. A registered causal condition encoder also predicts carry, opening/settling, deposited-retreat, or handle-ready stage with a masked auxiliary loss. This targets intermediate-state perturbations and release/retreat phase ambiguity rather than large rigid displacement.

assignment.subgoal: Carry the extracted block from above the tunnel to the open drawer, align it over the cavity, descend, open the gripper to leave the block resting at drawer-floor height, then retreat without disturbing it and reorient toward the drawer handle. Contact is maintained with the block until release. Approximate entry: block held high outside the tunnel, drawer open. Approximate exit: block resting in the open drawer near z=0.063 and x about -0.166 to -0.177 in the open-drawer world pose, gripper free and at/near the handle approach.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Compare FK of the IK target with the demonstrated commanded TCP pose after measured-current-TCP relative encode/decode, and compare unchanged gripper scalar. Maximum position metres, rotation radians and gripper error must be at most 0.005; rotation exp/log is exact on labels and nonunique IK joints are allowed.

contract.cut_relation: Covers all twelve complete [680,1160) assigned slices and retains both action-supervised overlaps. It refines the cut with fresh-state local Cartesian correction and a causal phase auxiliary loss, without changing the assigned carry, release, retreat or handle-transition responsibility.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [fresh-current-TCP-frame translation increment xyz in metres, fresh-current-TCP-frame rotation vector xyz in radians, native gripper scalar]. Training slot k uses inverse(measured TCP in that slot's pre-action observation) times the demonstrated commanded TCP pose. During sequential execution each of slots 1..8 is left-multiplied by the newly measured current world TCP pose, so increments are not accumulated open-loop from chunk start. panda_kinematics.solve_ik maps the resulting world TCP target to seven absolute joints from fresh qpos; the gripper scalar is appended unchanged. The four-class auxiliary head is training-only causal phase regularization and does not alter decoding or success criteria.
contract.parameter_semantics: The two pose-field arguments select the live observed block and drawer-goal world poses used for causal relative geometry, in metres and wxyz. phase_vocabulary selects the declared auxiliary classes: 0 carry/closed descent, 1 opening or settling, 2 deposited retreat, 3 handle-ready. The vocabulary is encoded in model input and is advisory rather than contact truth.
